## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

The menu describes elephant-apple chutney tempered with panch phutana. [Chef TZac: Odia cuisine is an evolved cuisine](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/blog-detail/chef-tzac-odia-cuisine-is-an-evolved-cuisine), Odia Experience menu, accompaniment paragraph. Mansita Mishra’s 27 November 2019 account of a chef and restaurant menu; contemporary interpretation, not a universal or current menu.

The Odisha summary lists Ouu khatta, but a later elephant-apple/jaggery entry is labelled Assam. That geography is unresolved. [Regional Cuisine of India, BHM-602AT](https://uou.ac.in/sites/default/files/slm/BHM-602AT.pdf), Printed p.131 / PDF p.131, Odisha summary; p.292 / PDF p.292, Oou Khatta entry. University teaching reference; one described version, not a definitive formula.

## A cook’s two versions and a remembered meal · reviewed 4 November 2026

In her 2017 sweet elephant-apple relish, Sasmita cooks and drains the fruit before moving it to another pan. Cumin and mustard seeds temper the oil; ginger, jaggery or sugar, and coconut follow. She also allows the cooked pieces to be crushed. Even within this recipe, texture is a choice.[^food-ou-sasmita2017]

Her 2019 sweet-and-sour version uses a mustard–cumin paste alongside panch phoron in the oil. She blends the paste separately; the whole spices go into hot oil before the cooked fruit is added. The precooked, drained fruit then meets the paste and jaggery. She suggests rice and dalma alongside it. These are two recipes by the same cook, offering variation rather than evidence from two households.[^food-ou-sasmita2019]

Julie Acharya Ray’s 2014 memoir places ou khatta in her mother’s Kartik meal. On banana leaves, rice and dal occupy the centre, with vegetable dishes and ou khatta around them. This is one family’s remembered arrangement, not a menu for every household.[^food-ou-ray2014]

The reviewed public narrative and visible source notes are recorded in [the food collection](collection.json) and [article metadata](ou-khatta-editorial.json). This reconciliation replaces the older summaries; it does not add a second public recipe account. Compare [Dalma](dalma.md). The attributed relish account offers rice and dalma as a serving combination; meal context, not universal ritual prescription.

The university’s Assam-labelled passage remains unresolved. These attributed accounts do not establish exclusive origin or make that other label an error. Recipe testing, locally contributed review, precise district distribution and current availability remain unverified.
